$comment: Each mutant is a real behaviour change to source that a test SHOULD detect.
A SURVIVED mutant means the suite cannot tell correct code from broken code.
This catalogue deliberately seeds the mutants that were found SURVIVING during
the 2026-09-30 adversarial test audit, so they can never silently regress:
• event-bus:B3 / B6  — regex anchoring and metachar escaping (both were gaps,
now killed by 3 added tests in event-bus.test.ts).
When adding a mutant, prefer semantically meaningful changes (inverted
comparisons, removed guards, wrong constants) over cosmetic ones.
`find` must appear verbatim in the source file and `replace` must differ.

mutants.why: Removing try/catch around handler dispatch regresses REL-004: one throwing subscriber silences every later one.
Errors isolated but never reported: failures become invisible to observability.
WAS A SURVIVOR. Removing ^...$ anchors lets an exact pattern match prefix/suffix variants.
Inverting the match predicate should fail essentially every dispatch test.
A no-op unsubscribe leaks subscriptions and double-delivers events.
WAS A SURVIVOR. Without escaping, '.' in a pattern becomes 'any char' and '+' becomes a quantifier.
A zero version floor accepts a genuinely-too-old corpus, reintroducing the original incident class.
Inverting the floor comparison rejects modern corpora and accepts ancient ones.
Dropping structural validation accepts malformed entities via an unchecked path.
An off-by-one in version comparison misorders every version pair.
Losing the equation-display class breaks every styled equation.
Breaking the section kind class breaks the whole structural DOM contract.
Text-only change: proves the assertions check rendered copy, not just element presence.
Loading-state copy is user-visible; a weakened test would miss it.
Flipping a boundary comparison breaks collision containment.
Removing damping makes walls perfectly elastic: bodies gain energy forever and never settle. A suite that only asserts 'vx flipped sign' cannot tell damping from no damping.
Dropping the giant_planet guard makes the sun tug on every body, changing the trajectory of the sun and of all non-planets. Only a test that asserts a NON-planet is unaffected will catch it.
mutants.find: if (body.type !== 'giant_planet' || body.isExploded || body.id === sun.id) return body;

mutants.why: Inverting the like/opposite-charge sign makes opposite charges repel and like charges attract — the single most consequential physics sign in the module.
Swapping the masses in the impulse formula breaks momentum exchange: the heavier body takes the lighter body's kick. A test asserting only 'velocities changed' will not notice.
mutants.find: const p = (2 * (nx * kx + ny * ky)) / (out1.mass + out2.mass);
mutants.replace: const p = (2 * (nx * kx + ny * ky)) / (out1.mass * out2.mass || 1);

mutants.why: Changing the minimum growth from 6 to 0 lets tiny bodies be devoured for effectively no growth, breaking the blackhole accretion model.
Changing the cosmic-view multiplier changes every force in the simulation. Caught only if a test asserts the exact multiplier rather than mere non-zero motion.
Removing the blackholeDisabled gate means a disabled blackhole still pulls and devours everything.
Changing the per-question award from 10 changes every score and every percentage. High blast radius: results, completion, and the emitted event all shift.
Removing the double-answer guard lets a learner re-answer the same question to farm score. This is a real integrity defect, not a cosmetic one.
Inverting correctness inverts the entire quiz. Should be trivially caught — its survival would indicate the suite is not exercising validateAnswer at all.
Off-by-one in completion detection either ends the quiz early or never ends it.
Math.floor instead of Math.round biases every percentage downward, which can push a learner below a grade boundary (see Q6).
Raising the Scholar boundary from 70 to 90 silently re-labels a genuinely proficient learner as a mere 'Great Attempt'. A boundary test at exactly 70 must exist to catch it.
Changing how totalQuestions is derived from maxScore reports the wrong question count on the results screen.
Collapsing the easy/medium/hard ladder by index removes progressive difficulty from every mapped lesson. Caught only if a test asserts the per-index difficulty, not just that questions exist.
Bypassing the subject map produces one lesson per question instead of one per subject — the core grouping contract of the mapper.
Using only the first question's time instead of the sum under-reports lesson length, which feeds scheduling and progress estimates.
mutants.find: const totalTime = qs.reduce((sum, q) => sum + q.estimatedTimeMinutes, 0);

mutants.why: Dropping the numeric sort leaves grade levels in first-seen order, so [11, 9, 10] renders as such. The existing test asserts toEqual([9,10,11]) and should kill it.
mutants.find: const gradeLevels = [...new Set(qs.flatMap((q) => q.gradeLevels))].sort((a, b) => a - b);
mutants.replace: const gradeLevels = [...new Set(qs.flatMap((q) => q.gradeLevels))].sort((a, b) => b - a);

mutants.why: Dropping the Set means duplicate tags accumulate across questions in a subject, inflating tag counts used for filtering.
Hardcoding the lesson id breaks the stable-identifier contract that deep-links and progress tracking depend on.
Dropping the explanation callout strips the pedagogical content from every mapped lesson while still looking structurally valid. The existing kind assertion should kill it.
